newsitem.title: USA: Hydro-Quebec, 3M funded for more battery research.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec, 3M funded for more battery research.

text.p: The United States Advanced Battery Consortium said Thursday it awarded a third contract to the partnership made up of Hydro-Quebec, Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co and Argonne National Laboratories to develope lithium polymer batteries for electric vehicles.
The two-year contract is worth $24.5 million. It brings the total value of the research and development work that USABC has awarded the partnership to $84.8 million since 1993.
The new contract covers research focused on cost and performance objectives established by USABC for the next generation of batteries for electric vehicles.

The contract calls for the assembly and delivery in 1998 of full-size lithium polymer battery packs for electric vehicle road testing. The total number of packs to be delivered, and their final specifications, are to be determined before the end of this year, the consortium said.

The "partnership is launching an important stage of LPB development that will make possible in the coming decade the commercialization of electric vehicles having performances in power, range and cost approaching those of vehicles equipped with internal combustion engines, while meeting the most stringent safety standards," said Michel Gauthier, LPB program manager at Hydro-Quebec.

The consortium is made up of the three big U.S. auto makers -- Ford Motor Co, Chrysler Corp and General Motors Corp -- and the Electric Power Research Institute. It is partially funded by the US Department of Energy and is responsible for accelerating research and development on batteries for electric vehicles.
